extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and parties to inter partes reexamination (patent owners and third-party requesters)
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO/MPEP guidance for evaluating requests to order and conduct inter partes reexamination: standards for granting or denying, procedural timelines, what prior art may be considered, filing/petition requirements, and processing steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for vacating a reexamination order
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasons that may justify vacating a reexamination order (examples listed A–F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes situations such as: a final decision of a Federal Court after all appeals; reexamination ordered for the wrong patent; reexamination ordered based on a duplicate copy of the request; or the reexamination order was based wholly on the same question of patentability raised by prior art previously considered in an earlier concluded examination of the patent (e.g., the application which matured into the patent, a prior reexamination, an interference proceeding). See also In re Recreative Technologies Corp., 83 F.3d 1394, 38 USPQ2d 1776 (Fed. Cir. 1996) and MPEP § 2642 II.A for vacating criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to 37 CFR 1.181 petition (timing and format)
rubrics_metrics.description: When a 37 CFR 1.181 petition to vacate a reexamination order is filed, the third party requester may file a single submission in opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any opposition must be filed within two weeks of the date a copy of the 1.181 petition was served on the third party requester to ensure consideration (reexaminations are conducted with special dispatch per 35 U.S.C. 314(c)). Advisable practices: immediately notify the CRU SPE by telephone that an opposition will be filed and, whenever possible, submit the opposition by facsimile transmission. Filing of a 1.181 petition to vacate an ultra vires reexamination order is limited to a single submission even if a third party opposition is filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of prior art submitted after reexamination order
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior art citations submitted under 37 CFR 1.501 after the date of the order should be retained separately until the reexamination proceeds concludes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such submissions should be retained in a separate file by the Technology Center (usually the TC Quality Assurance Specialist) and stored until conclusion of the proceeding, at which time the prior art citation is entered of record in the patent file. Note 37 CFR 1.902 governs submissions by patent owners and third party requesters after reexamination has been ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial standard — No substantial new question of patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for inter partes reexamination will be denied if a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ) is not found based on patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner concludes no SNQ has been raised, prepare a decision denying the request (use Form paragraph 26.02 as introductory paragraph). The decision should explain, for each patent or publication cited in the request, why the citation is: (A) cumulative to art cited in earlier concluded examination; (B) not available against the claims (e.g., due to date or not a publication); (C) would not be important to a reasonable examiner (even if available and not cumulative); or (D) was cited in the patent record and is barred by MPEP § 2642 II.A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision content requirements and treatment of arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Content the examiner must include in a decision denying reexamination and how to treat non-patent/prior-art arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision must respond to the substance of each argument raised by the third party requester which is based on patents or printed publications. Arguments based on grounds not based on prior art patents or printed publications (e.g., public use or on-sale under 35 U.S.C. 102(b), abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c)) are improper for reexamination and should be noted as not considered or commented upon (see 37 CFR 1.906(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference procedure for denial
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing a final order denying reexamination, the examiner notifies the CRU SPE who convenes a panel review conference to review the proposed denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conference confirms the preliminary decision, the order denying reexamination shall be issued and signed by the examiner with two other conferees initialing as 'conferee' to indicate presence. If the panel does not confirm the preliminary decision, the examiner should reevaluate and issue an appropriate communication. See MPEP § 2671.03 for panel composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question (SNQ) — what raises SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination is granted if a substantial new question of patentability is raised by the request based on patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An SNQ exists when cited art presents teaching not present in prior prosecution/previous examinations and a reasonable examiner would consider that teaching important in deciding patentability of the claim(s). Examples in MPEP: a reference teaching a spring-supported extruder at a 30° angle when that teaching was not present in prior prosecution could raise an SNQ for certain claims. Conversely, a reference that is a substantial equivalent of art considered earlier or cumulative will not raise an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limited to claims identified in request
rubrics_metrics.description: Only claims for which reexamination is requested will be reexamined; claims not requested remain not reexamined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request does not seek reexamination for certain claims, those claims will not be reexamined (example: 'reexamination has not been requested for claims 5–20; accordingly claims 5–20 will not be reexamined').

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time and comment periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on extensions of time and third-party comment deadlines in inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) are not permitted in inter partes reexamination (those provisions apply only to 'an applicant'). Patent owner extensions are provided by 37 CFR 1.956. Third party requester comments have a statutory 30-day comment period from service of the patent owner’s response and extensions of time are not available for these comments (35 U.S.C. 314(b)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to apprise Office of ongoing litigations or proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent owner (and third party requester) must notify the Office of any litigation or other proceeding involving the patent during reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remind patent owner of continuing responsibility under 37 CFR 1.985(a) to apprise the Office of litigation activity or other prior/concurrent proceedings throughout the reexamination. Third party requesters may likewise apprise the Office. See MPEP §§ 2686 and 2686.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerical and legal-advisor processing steps and timelines after decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative processing after an examiner prepares and signs the decision (grant or denial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case is forwarded to CRU clerical staff who prepare decision/Office action for mailing and make copies of prior art not supplied by requester (one copy for patent owner, one for requester). File and decision forwarded to CRU SPE and then to Reexamination Legal Advisor (RLA) for review within nine weeks of the filing date of the request (unless authorized otherwise). CRU support staff prints headings, attaches documents, mails decisions, annotates files, updates scanning and PALM entries, and makes reexamination e-file record entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition from denial — timing and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Third party requester may petition Director to review a denial of reexamination under 37 CFR 1.927 and 1.181 within one month of mailing date of the examiner's determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must comply with § 1.181(b). If no petition is timely filed or the petition decision affirms the denial, the determination is final and nonappealable. If a petition is filed timely, the petition (with the reexamination file) is forwarded to the CRU Director who reviews de novo. A decision on petition is final and not appealable. If petition granted, the CRU Director should include sentence that an Office action will be mailed in due course. After petition is granted the CRU SPE will ordinarily reassign the reexamination to another examiner (per 37 CFR 1.931(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassignment policy after petition grant
rubrics_metrics.description: When a petition under 37 CFR 1.927 is granted, reexamination will normally be conducted by another examiner; reassignment is the general rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under normal circumstances reexamination will not be reassigned to a primary/assistant examiner who was involved in any part of the original examination of the patent or its parent. The CRU Director may make exceptions only in unusual circumstances (e.g., no other examiner available with adequate knowledge).

rubrics_metrics.name: General conduct rules — applicability of initial examination procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination is conducted according to procedures established for initial examination under sections 132 and 133, except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may propose any amendment and new claims except those enlarging claim scope. Except for the reexamination request itself, any document filed by either party shall be served on the other. Office will send requester copies of communications to patent owner. Third party requester has one opportunity to file written comments addressing issues raised by Office action or patent owner response if received within 30 days of service. All proceedings are to be conducted with special dispatch unless Director determines good cause to suspend (35 U.S.C. 314(c); 37 CFR 1.937). All communications directed to merits must be in writing and filed for entry into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive notice and effect of undelivered order
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination proceeds even if the order is returned undelivered because notice under 37 CFR 1.11(c) is constructive notice to the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of response from the patent owner will not delay reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: CFR sections governing examination and reexamination certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination is conducted in accordance with 37 CFR 1.104, 1.105, 1.110–1.116 and will result in issuance of a reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.997, except as otherwise provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings are to be conducted with special dispatch per 35 U.S.C. 314(c). Patent owner and third party requester will be sent copies of all Office actions and must serve copies of their submissions on each other. Citations of art on patent file prior to order will be considered by examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who reexamines (assignment of examiner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily the same patent examiner who decided whether to grant the request will conduct the examination; exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.927 is granted, reexamination will normally be conducted by another examiner. Reassignment to the original examiner is generally avoided unless no other capable examiner is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of prior art to be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must consider patents and printed publications from multiple sources when conducting reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sources include: (A) cited by another reexamination requester under 37 CFR 1.510 or 1.915; (B) cited by patent owner under duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.933) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.98; (C) discovered by examiner in searching; (D) of record in patent file from earlier examination; (E) of record from any 37 CFR 1.501 submission prior to date of order if it complies with 37 CFR 1.98; and (F) cited by third party requester under appropriate circumstances pursuant to 37 CFR 1.948. Where parties submit citations in compliance with the rules, the degree of consideration normally depends on how well the submitting party has explained content and relevance. Examiner initials on PTO/SB/08A or 08B do not indicate consideration beyond that explanation unless record shows otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of consideration for file references and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent of examiner consideration of references from the patent file depends on availability of the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reference (other than a U.S. patent or U.S. patent application publication) is not scanned into the Image File Wrapper (IFW), what was said about that reference in the patent’s record is the full extent of consideration unless parties appropriately supply a copy. Parties should supply copies when necessary for proper consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required copies under 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting references, a legible copy is required for certain categories of documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required copies include: (1) each foreign patent; (2) each publication or the portion that caused it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required by the Office); (3) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including the claims and any drawing or that portion that caused it to be listed; and (4) all other information or the portion which caused it to be listed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting copies of copending reexamination proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties should not submit copies of copending reexamination proceedings and applications that could be mistaken for a new request or filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instead of copies, submitters may provide the application/proceeding number and its status. Submissions not permitted entry may be returned, expunged, or discarded at Office discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for submitting new art after NIRC or during printing cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: After the Notice of Intent to Issue Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) has been mailed or when the reexamination has entered the printing cycle, submissions by the patent owner of patents/printed publications or other 1.98(a) information are subject to stringent requirements for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions made after NIRC must be accompanied by (A) a factual accounting explaining why the information could not have been submitted earlier, and (B) an explanation of the relevance of the information to the claimed invention in the proceeding. Entry and consideration require a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 with fee. If the proceeding is in the printing cycle, the patent owner must also provide an unequivocal statement that one or more claims are unpatentable, an amendment to such claim(s), and an explanation how the amendment causes the claim(s) to be patentable. The petition must show the requisite basis for interrupting special dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of prior art in the reexamination request and on PTO forms
rubrics_metrics.description: The reexamination request must provide a listing of patents and printed publications in accordance with 37 CFR 1.98; examiner must record prior art on official forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must list on PTO-892 (if not already listed on PTO/SB/08A, 08B, or PTO/SB/42 or equivalent) all prior art patents/printed publications cited in the decision, applied in making rejections, or cited as pertinent during proceedings. Citations listed on PTO-892 and those not struck through on other forms will be printed on the reexamination certificate under 'References cited.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of inter partes reexamination (37 CFR 1.906)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines substantive scope and limits of issues that may be resolved in inter partes reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims will be examined on the basis of patents or printed publications and, with respect to subject matter added or deleted during reexamination, on the basis of 35 U.S.C. 112 requirements. Claims may not be amended to enlarge their scope. Issues other than those indicated (patents/printed publications and 112 for added matter) will not be resolved in inter partes reexamination; if such issues arise they should be noted and patent owner may consider filing a reissue application. Inter partes differs from ex parte in procedural matters (party participation, types/timing of Office actions, estoppel effects, initiation prohibitions) but not in substance to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bases for reexamination rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejections in reexamination proceedings may only be made on specific grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejections may only be made on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications, or double patenting. The same decisions cited in MPEP §§ 2258 and 2258.01 for determining presence/absence of an SNQ in ex parte reexamination apply equally to inter partes reexamination because statutory language is shared.
